subject: general
question: When we observe the floor of a swimming pool filled with water we notice that the pool looks:

options.text: less deep than it actually is
More wider than it actually is
less wide than it actually is

solution:
The correct answer is __**less deep than it actually is.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 When viewed directly above, swimming pools appear shallower than they actually are due to light **reflection **at the **water's surface**.
 
 
• 
 The reason for this is that the light rays **emanating **from the **submerged **item do not **strike **us directly.
 
 
• 
 As long as the light is in the water, it goes **straight**; however, if the light exits the water **obliquely **into the air, it is bent downward toward the surface.
 
 
• 
 **Refraction **is the term for this **bending**, which happens whenever **light travels **through one **transparent medium **and then into **another **that has a **different density**.
 
 
• 
 Our eyes do not **account **for **refraction**; instead, they determine the **object's position **as though the light had come from a **straight line**.
 
 
• 
 Light accelerates once again as it leaves a **liquid **or **piece **of **glass **and **enters **the **air**.
 
 
• 
 It will **refract away **from the **normal **if it encounters the **glass-air interface **at any angle other than** 0°.**
 
 
• 
 This is accurate for **small **angles, however as the **angles increase**, something else occurs.
 
 
• 
 Because of this, **swimming pools **seem to get **shallower **as you approach the end that is **farthest **from you.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Refraction **in physics is the redirection of a wave as it **travels **through one **medium **and then **another**.
 
• A **change **in the **medium **or a change in the **wave's speed **might both result in a **redirection**.
 
• Although refraction of **light waves **is the most frequently **seen phenomenon**, refraction can also occur with **sound waves **and **water waves**.
 
• The wave speed change and the **initial wave propagation** direction in relation to the wave speed change both affect how much a wave is refracted.
